chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Dizzy Gillespie and the spitball firing from Cab's band
summary: The Cab Jivers and the spitball incident that got Dizzy fired.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: I read somewhere that he was not too fond of Dizzy's playing.

Well not too many people were then, you know, because I know Cab used to say, now the trumpet players in the band idolized Dizzy for what he was doing, but Cab there when Diz was with Cab you know, he'd get up there and Cab couldn't dig him too well, you know, he's up there playing. And then a lot of times maybe another trumpet player, Shad Collins or Jonah would come up and play a solo

maybe after Quinten Jackson or one of them and come up and they would be influenced by Dizzy a little, and Cab would look at them, look at Jonah and say oh man, you too, have you gone on that wagon too? And not too many but look what he is today.
Do you remember the night that Dizzy got fired?

Yeah, I was right there in the band. See, we had a little thing they called them the Cab Jivers, we used to go down front, play, Tyree Glenn, Milt Hinton, me, and Chu. And four of us in front of the bandstand. Well while we would be in front, see, the band in back of us would be blacked out and there would be just pin spots on us. Well, Diz and Jonah and all them sitting back there in that bandstand, they all crazy back there, they used to get spitballs and throw at the back of our heads and everything, with a rubber band, boom, you know, it'd hit you maybe on your head, you'd jump. You can't look around, you know, and but this day all of them was up there cutting the fool and Cab happened to be looking out the wing and saw them. Saw this spitball come through there. Diz was so fast that he did it and got back, so when Cab looked, Diz was sitting still. But Jonah's the one did it.
Milt Hinton claims that he did it.
No Milt was down there with us. And so, Diz was sitting--Diz is the one did it. No he wasn't, it
was Jonah, it could have been Milt.
Milt claimed that he did it. But that Cab blamed Dizzy.

Yeah, because Diz was always up there fooling around. And so one word led on to another after the curtain closed. 'You're a damn liar it wasn't me.' 'You're a damn liar it was you,' and one word led on to another, it wasn't that severe about all that cutting and all that, because Benny Payne stopped it you know.

No, not all that. It wasn't that. Maybe Diz had a knife in his hand, but it wasn't all that. But you know how they can build up a big story. And that was it. And Diz was fired. And the next week we were at the Apollo Theatre and Diz was sitting right up in the front row.
